passages.text: SYPHILIS, or LUES VENEREA, the venereal disease, a contagious distemper communicated chiefly by impure coition with an infected person.
It is generally believed to have been brought into Europe from America by the sailors of Columbus, and to have first appeared at the siege of Naples in 1495.
Mr John Hunter holds that the gonorrhoea and the chancre arise from one and the same poison, which produces the one or the other according to the part it falls upon.
The first sign is commonly a small ulcer called a chancre; the poison afterwards enters the blood, and shows itself by eruptions on the skin and ulcers of the throat.
If neglected, it at length attacks the bones, causing nocturnal pains and nodes, and may destroy the bones of the nose and palate.
Mercury is the only certain remedy; it is given by the mouth or rubbed into the skin, till the gums become sore and a salivation is raised.
Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum subspecies pallidum.
The infection develops in stages: primary, secondary, latent and tertiary. The primary stage usually presents as a single painless chancre, a firm ulcer at the site of infection.
Secondary syphilis brings a widespread rash, which often includes the palms and soles, and may cause sores in the mouth.
Tertiary syphilis can appear years after infection. It may cause soft growths called gummas, and can damage the heart and the nervous system (neurosyphilis).

The origin of syphilis is disputed. One hypothesis holds that sailors on the voyages of Christopher Columbus carried it from the Americas to Europe; another holds that it was present in Europe before. The first well-recorded European outbreak was in 1494 and 1495 in Naples.
For a long time gonorrhea and syphilis were thought to be one disease. In the 1830s Philippe Ricord showed that they are separate diseases.
Mercury was used for centuries but had serious toxic side effects. Since the 1940s the first-line treatment has been penicillin.

reasons: Rare terms appear in both: chancre, Columbus, Naples, mercury.

alignments.label: From America

britannica.quote: brought into Europe from America by the sailors of Columbus

wikipedia.quote: The origin of syphilis is disputed

alignments.note: The 1797 text gives one hypothesis as settled. It is still one of two main views.

britannica.quote: first appeared at the siege of Naples in 1495

alignments.label: One poison

britannica.quote: the gonorrhoea and the chancre arise from one and the same poison

alignments.note: Change in knowledge. Hunter's view was given up after Ricord's work.

alignments.label: Chancre

britannica.quote: a small ulcer called a chancre

alignments.note: Same first sign and the same term.

alignments.label: Rash and throat

britannica.quote: eruptions on the skin and ulcers of the throat

alignments.note: The second stage is described in the same way.

alignments.label: Late stage

wikipedia.quote: can damage the heart and the nervous system

alignments.note: Damage to bone does occur. The 1797 text does not know the late damage to heart and brain.

alignments.label: Mercury

britannica.quote: Mercury is the only certain remedy

alignments.note: Change in knowledge. Mercury poisons the patient and does not cure the infection. Penicillin does.

alignments.label: A bacterium

wikipedia.quote: caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum

alignments.note: The 1797 text speaks of a poison. The bacterium was found in 1905.

Did syphilis come from America?.answer: The 1797 entry says so, naming the sailors of Columbus [B2]. Wikipedia says the origin is disputed: one hypothesis supports the Columbus route and another says the disease was already in Europe [W5]. Both texts agree on the outbreak at Naples in the 1490s [B2] [W5].

How was syphilis treated in 1797?.answer: With mercury, given by mouth or rubbed into the skin until the gums became sore [B6]. Wikipedia says mercury had serious toxic side effects and that penicillin has been the first-line treatment since the 1940s [W7].
